prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "user_guide", with the standing line "The reader's manual for the Poetry Application: how to install it, then where its words, links and reports live." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows The application window drawn open and sectioned, sidebar of destinations along its left inside edge, Dashboard panel at its centre showing tallies of items and links, and the Command Palette floating as a small search box over everything. Thin routes run from the sidebar to each destination panel; one bolder route leaps from the palette directly to a destination, bypassing the sidebar.

Magnified circles set beside it show first circle, the Graph view magnified so round nodes and the lines between them are separable. second circle, the palette's typed box showing a jump straight to a page. third circle, the theme switch in two states. studies, the download, the two operating systems' install gestures, and the first-run setup that builds the local database.

Colour is used so that warm accent, the reader's own path through the application; cool accent, links between items; single bright accent, the keyboard shortcut route.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: three installation steps before first use; two operating systems supported; five parts to an item's page; three reports listed; two themes.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: Search on the entry route; Item Page on the opened entry; Definition, Rich Content, Media, Text-to-Speech, Derivation and Appendices on the parts of that entry; Graph on the node-and-edge drawing; nodes and edges on the shapes themselves; Reports on the lists of missing definitions and orphaned items; Tables on the raw data drawer; Items, Links and Cliches on the table drawers; Command Palette on the floating box, with Cmd+K and Ctrl+K on the keys that summon it; Settings on the theme switch, Light and Dark on its two states; Dashboard on the centre panel, Total Items and Total Links on its tallies; Poetry Maker.app and Windows installer on the two install studies; First Run on the setup that builds the local database.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: Dashboard, Search, Item Page, Graph, Reports, Tables, Settings, Command Palette, Cmd+K, Ctrl+K nodes, edges, jump to page, Light, Dark Poetry Maker.app, Windows installer, First Run, local database Definition, Rich Content, Media, Derivation, Appendices, Text-to-Speech Items, Links, Cliches, Total Items, missing definitions, orphaned items

Set these short notes beside what they explain: Search is the way in; Sidebar reaches every page; Palette searches without leaving the page Graph view is still experimental; Nodes are words and authors First run initialises the local database One selected item, read in full Tables show the raw database; Reports list the gaps
